The grader is a model, not a person. qwen3.8-27b graded every answer. It once wrote a grade that contradicted its own reasoning; it now reasons first, but it is still not perfect. The spot-check sheets (bench/spotcheck_v1.md, bench/spotcheck_v2.md) let a person measure how often it is wrong. That audit has not been done yet.

Generated questions are easier than real ones. Most come from a single section and name their subject. Real users ask vaguer questions. The overview (15) and two-section (22 and 30) groups are small, so one answer moves them by 3–7 points.

Fixes were developed on the first test set. The improvements on that set are partly fitted to it. The held-out set was written afterwards, on different sections, to check that the fixes generalise; it has no overview questions.

Some gold labels were wrong. 5 of 30 (first set) and 4 of 30 (held-out) questions the generator called unanswerable are in fact answered by the document. An audit step found them, and they are excluded from all numbers.
Where plain RAG is still ahead. On the first set, plain RAG refuses unanswerable questions slightly more often (88% vs 80%). On the held-out set we are ahead (92% vs 88%).

OCR on heavily damaged Indic scans is still unreadable by every engine we tried. Such pages are now marked unreadable instead of filled with invented text. The OCR test uses synthetic damage on 3 pages per language; real scans with typed ground truth would be a better test.
Speed depends on the API tier. Times were measured on Groq's paid tier. On the free tier, rate limits stretch a typical answer to about 7 seconds.

Competitors were not run. Section 2 describes them from public documentation. The baseline uses our small e5 embedder without a reranker; commercial systems use larger embedders and rerankers, so they would be stronger than this baseline.
